title: attestation: Prepare provider and instance core
overview: Introduces the attestation core module: the public provider descriptor (include/linux/attestation.h), the private instance object (core/internal.h) and the registry, validation and lifecycle code (core/core.c) that implement the generated base-family callbacks. Provider drivers depend on the header; core.c depends on the generated CTLV header from patch 14. Journal storage follows in patch 16 and CTLV operation handlers in patch 17, so CONFIG_ATTESTATION is not yet wired into a parent Kconfig.

files.purpose: Driver-API document describing how a provider registers with the attestation family and how teardown is ordered. Linked from the driver-api index.

units.title: Overview of the subsystem
units.summary: States that providers appear as descendants of the ctlv-attestation family and split ownership between core and provider.
units.details: The core owns evidence retrieval, MR topology and the append-only journal; providers own native hardware access and immutable capability descriptions.

units.title: Registering a provider
units.summary: Explains the descriptor, the pre_init hand-off and the per-instance mutex that serializes operations.
units.details:
- The provider passes `struct attestation_provider` to the base family via the generated `pre_init`.
- Family-wide op hooks delegate to `ctlv_attestation_op_pre()`/`ctlv_attestation_op_post()`, which take and drop `att->lock`.
- Descriptor and MR storage must stay valid until `ctlv_destroy()` or failed-creation unwind.

units.title: Teardown
units.summary: Documents the teardown order: drain operations, withdraw from the registry in pre_fini, stop events, then fini.
units.details: This matches `ctlv_attestation_pre_fini()` and `ctlv_attestation_fini()` in core.c.

units.summary: Links the new attestation.rst right after the ctlv document.

files.purpose: Core of the attestation module: validates provider descriptors, keeps a global registry of instances, and implements the generated base-family lifecycle and operation-hook callbacks. It is called by CTLV (init, post_init, pre_fini, fini, op_pre/op_post) and by provider drivers through the base family, and calls the generated provide/enable helpers.

units.title: Header, includes and registry state
units.summary: Includes plus the global xarray of instances, the registry mutex and the next-index counter.
units.details: `attestation_instances` maps a monotonically increasing index to each `struct attestation`; `attestation_registry_lock` serializes index allocation and insertion.

units.title: attestation_algorithm_valid()
units.summary: Accepts only known hash algorithms with a nonzero digest size that fits HASH_MAX_DIGESTSIZE.
units.details: Used by MR property validation.

units.title: attestation_mr_props_validate()
units.summary: Checks one fixed MR descriptor: name, strictly ascending valid algorithm list, and that readable/extendable flags have matching provider callbacks.
units.details: Strictly ascending order makes the algorithm list unique and gives digest sets a canonical order. Limits (name length 128, up to 21 algorithms) mirror the schema.

units.title: attestation_evidence_caps_validate()
units.summary: Validates evidence capabilities and their consistency with the evidence_get callback.
units.details:
- No caps requires no `evidence_get`; caps require it.
- Bounds on object count, challenge lengths and total output are checked.
- Each object needs a bounded, non-empty, unique format name and a length within the total.

units.title: attestation_provider_validate()
units.summary: Top-level check of a provider descriptor, run once at core init.
units.details: Calls the evidence caps and per-MR validators, and requires mrs/mrs_count to agree and MR callbacks to be accompanied by MRs. Declared in internal.h.

units.title: attestation_parent_exists()
units.summary: Scans the registry for an instance already attached to the same parent device.
units.details: Enforces one attestation instance per parent device. Called with the xarray lock held from `attestation_registry_insert()`.

units.title: attestation_registry_insert() and remove()
units.summary: Allocates the next index, reserves a slot, then atomically checks for a duplicate parent and stores the instance.
units.details:
- Under the registry mutex the slot is reserved with GFP_KERNEL so the later store under the xa lock can use GFP_NOWAIT without failing.
- A duplicate parent erases the reservation and returns -EEXIST.
- On success `att->index` is set and the counter advances.
- The entry is stored without ATTESTATION_REGISTERED; `attestation_registry_remove()` erases it.

units.title: Registered mark helpers
units.summary: Query and clear the ATTESTATION_REGISTERED xarray mark that says an instance accepts operations.
units.details: Both require `att->lock` held. The mark is set in `ctlv_attestation_post_init()` and cleared by `attestation_stop()` or `ctlv_attestation_pre_fini()`.

units.title: attestation_provide_ops()
units.summary: Marks the evidence-get operation as provided and enabled when the provider has evidence capabilities.
units.details: Uses the generated `ctlv_attestation_evidence_get_provide/enable` helpers so CTLV advertises only operations the provider supports.

units.title: attestation_core_init() and fini()
units.summary: Initializes an instance: validate provider, init lock, register in the xarray, enable ops; fini undoes it.
units.details:
- `att->initialized` records successful registration so `attestation_core_fini()` only removes registered entries.
- Fini is idempotent via the `ctlvdev` NULL check, so the error path in init can reuse it.
- Registered mark is not set yet; that waits for post_init.

units.title: Generated base-family callbacks
units.summary: Implements the lifecycle callbacks the generated family calls: priv_size, init, post_init, pre_fini, fini.
units.details:
- `init_info` is the provider descriptor passed through pre_init.
- post_init sets ATTESTATION_REGISTERED, making the instance visible to operations.
- pre_fini clears it while CTLV events still work; fini releases the core state.

units.title: Operation hooks
units.summary: op_pre takes the instance mutex and rejects operations on unregistered instances; op_post releases it.
units.details: Providers' family-wide hooks delegate here, so the mutex covers the native callback, journal commit and event emission. op_pre returns -ENODEV with the lock dropped; on success the lock is held until op_post.

units.title: Module init/exit and metadata
units.summary: Trivial module init; exit asserts the registry is empty and destroys the xarray.
units.details: MODULE_IMPORT_NS("CTLV") gives access to the CTLV exported symbols.

files.purpose: Private header shared by core files: the instance structure and internal function prototypes. Included by core.c and later by journal and op-handler files.

units.title: Includes and ATTESTATION_REGISTERED
units.summary: Include guard, dependencies including the generated CTLV header, and the xarray mark used for registration.

units.title: struct attestation
units.summary: The per-instance private object stored in CTLV priv: device, provider descriptor, registry index, lock and init flag.
units.details: `lock` guards mutable instance state and serializes operations; `provider` is immutable and owned by the provider driver.

units.title: Internal prototypes
units.summary: Declarations for core init/fini, registered-state helpers, provider validation and op enabling.

files.purpose: Public API for provider drivers: the immutable descriptors and callbacks a provider supplies. The generated base family and core.c consume them; later patches (TDX provider) implement them.

units.title: Header and digest types
units.summary: Includes, forward declarations, and the digest and digest-set types used by MR callbacks.
units.details: A digest set is ordered the same way as the MR's algorithm list.

units.title: struct attestation_mr_props
units.summary: Immutable description of one measurement register: id, name, ordered algorithms, optional native index, and readable/extendable flags.

units.title: Evidence capability and request types
units.summary: Types describing what evidence a provider can produce and the validated request and result passed to its callback.
units.details: Caps list supported formats and bounds; a request carries the challenge and resolved output blobs, and the result reports the length produced per object.

units.title: struct attestation_provider
units.summary: The provider descriptor: native callbacks (evidence_get, mr_read, mr_extend) plus immutable evidence caps and fixed MR array.
units.details: Validated by `attestation_provider_validate()`; callbacks receive the `struct attestation` and run under its lock.
